result.rationale: In the diff, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when credential sharing is enabled (it returns `response` from `fetch(...)` directly, with no `.json()` or axios wrapping), while in the non-sharing path it returns the axios response. The zoho-bigin CalendarService then does `if (!tokenInfo.data.error)`, expecting the axios shape; a fetch Response has no `data` property, so this would throw a TypeError in sharing mode. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: In sharing mode tokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, but line 95 evaluates tokenInfo.data.error expecting the axios response shape. Response.data is undefined, so if (!tokenInfo.data.error) throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error') — every Zoho Bigin calendar operation crashes whenever credential sharing is enabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `tokenInfo` is now obtained via `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then used as if it were an Axios response (`if (!tokenInfo.data.error)`). But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy. A `fetch` Response has no `.data`, so `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `tokenInfo.data.error` will throw a `TypeError`. This matches the finding and is directly implied by the diff.
